audits.mathematicalReason: Drop perpendiculars from B and C to AD. The two end right triangles have equal hypotenuses AB and CD and equal heights 3, so HL makes their horizontal legs equal. Each horizontal leg is (16 − 8)/2 = 4. Pythagoras gives AB = CD = √(3² + 4²) = 5, hence the perimeter is 16 + 8 + 5 + 5 = 34. The assessed theorem and both supporting scopes fit this valid route.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let the acute tip angle be a and the acute notch angle be b = a + 10°. The polygon interior angle at a notch is 360° − b. Thus the interior-angle sum gives n[a + (360° − b)] = (2n − 2)180°, or 350n = 360n − 360. Therefore n = 36. The polygon-angle-sum scope applies to this simple concave polygon, and angle subtraction supplies the stated support.

figureEvidence.fact: The boundary alternates outward tips A_i and inward notches B_i. The small acute angle at a B_i is the notch opening, not the reflex interior angle of the star.

audits.mathematicalReason: Normalize each large square to side length 1. In I, each shaded triangle has perpendicular legs 1/2 and 1/2, so the total shaded area is 2(1/8) = 1/4. In II, the shaded square has area (1/2)² = 1/4. In III, each shaded diamond has horizontal and vertical diagonals of length 1/2; splitting it into triangles gives area 1/8. The two diamonds therefore total 1/4. Composite-area decomposition, supported by triangle and square areas, correctly describes this route.

This is a valid three-set inclusion-exclusion route, including the required check of empty and higher-order intersections.

audits.mathematicalReason: Writing angle A = a gives a + 4a + 4a = 180°, so a = 20°. The intercepted minor arc BC and its central angle measure 40° by the inscribed angle theorem. Since B and C are adjacent vertices of the regular polygon, this central angle is 360°/n. Hence n = 360/40 = 9. The circle and regular-polygon scopes fit, with the triangle angle sum supporting the calculation.

The thousands unit cancels in each ratio. Percentage-growth applications and reading numerical scales are appropriate assessed and supporting scopes.

audits.mathematicalReason: For N tiles with I shared unit edges, count tile-side incidences to obtain 4N = P + 2I. Initially I = (4·8 − 14)/2 = 9. Each added tile shares at least one edge with the original figure, so the new shared-edge count is at least 11. With 10 tiles, P = 40 − 2I is even and at most 18, excluding every listed alternative except 18. This value is attainable: put one tile directly above the leftmost upper-row tile and another directly above the rightmost upper-row tile. Each shares exactly one original edge, and they do not share an edge with each other. The candidate's incidence double-counting scope is valid.

figureEvidence.fact: The original figure has two rows of four unit squares, with the upper row shifted one unit to the right relative to the lower row.
The top edges of the leftmost and rightmost upper-row tiles are exposed and sufficiently separated to attach two new tiles above them without the new tiles sharing an edge.
